name: Lorenz gauge ↔ harmonic gauge in linearized gravity
summary: Linearized GR is a gauge theory of h_{μν} with δh_{μν} = ∂_μξ_ν + ∂_νξ_μ; in Lorenz (de Donder) gauge the trace-reversed perturbation obeys a sourced wave equation solved by retarded potentials exactly like A^μ, and the residual gauge freedom gives TT gauge with two transverse polarizations, as Coulomb/radiation gauge does for light.
breaks: The field is rank 2 (helicity ±2 vs ±1); the gauge group is linearized diffeomorphisms, which beyond linear order become non-abelian and act on spacetime itself; source conservation ∂T = 0 is consistent only at linear order.

name: Ashtekar variables: GR as an SU(2) gauge theory
summary: Ashtekar recast GR's phase space as an SU(2) connection A^i_a conjugate to a densitized triad E^a_i that acts as a non-abelian 'electric field'; loop quantum gravity then quantizes Wilson-loop holonomies and electric fluxes, so area becomes discrete like quantized flux lines.
breaks: Gravity adds the Hamiltonian and diffeomorphism constraints, which have no Yang–Mills counterpart, and the Barbero–Immirzi parameter γ; discrete area is a prediction of the quantization, not of the gauge-theory form.

name: Einstein–Maxwell theory: charged black holes
summary: The traceless Maxwell stress–energy tensor sources Einstein's equations; solving the coupled Einstein–Maxwell system gives the Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman black holes, with inner and outer horizons and an extremal limit Q = M in geometrized units.

name: Kaluza–Klein: Maxwell from five-dimensional gravity
summary: Compactifying 5D general relativity on a circle turns the off-diagonal metric components g_{μ5} into a U(1) gauge field obeying Maxwell's equations, with charge as momentum around the circle and gauge transformations as reparametrizations of the extra coordinate; it is the template for gauge fields from geometry in string compactifications.
map: ds_5^2=g_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu dx^\nu+\phi^2(dy+\kappa A_\mu dx^\mu)^2;\ y\to y-\kappa\lambda\Leftrightarrow A_\mu\to A_\mu+\partial_\mu\lambda
breaks: An extra radion scalar φ appears and must be stabilized; charge quantization ties e to the circle radius, and the minimal theory cannot produce chiral fermions, which string theory gets from richer compactifications.

name: Covariant Lorentz force as relativistic dynamics
summary: The covariant Lorentz force dp^μ/dτ = qF^{μν}u_ν is the prototype relativistic equation of motion: the antisymmetry of F keeps u·u fixed, so rest mass is conserved, and it gives the relativistic cyclotron frequency qB/(γm) that forced the move from cyclotrons to synchrotrons.

name: E and B as components of one Lorentz tensor
summary: Under a boost E and B mix as components of the antisymmetric tensor F^{μν} = ∂^μA^ν − ∂^νA^μ, so magnetism is electrostatics seen from a moving frame; E² − c²B² and E·B are the Lorentz invariants that classify fields.
map: F'^{\mu\nu}=\Lambda^\mu{}_\alpha\Lambda^\nu{}_\beta F^{\alpha\beta};\ \mathbf E'_\perp=\gamma(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)_\perp,\ \mathbf E'_\parallel=\mathbf E_\parallel
sources: Einstein (1905). "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper". *Ann. Phys.* 322, 891. [doi:10.1002/andp.19053221004](https://doi.org/10.1002/andp.19053221004)

name: Membrane paradigm: horizon as a 377 Ω conductor
summary: For external static observers the stretched horizon behaves as a 2D conducting membrane whose surface charges and currents terminate field lines, with surface resistivity equal to the impedance of free space; a charge lowered toward a hole has its field lines drawn onto the horizon like the induced charge on a conducting sphere.
breaks: The membrane is a fictitious bookkeeping surface with no charge carriers, and it is teleological: it responds to fields before they arrive. The description fails for observers falling through the horizon.

name: Fresnel drag as relativistic velocity addition
summary: Fizeau (1851) found that light in flowing water is dragged by the fraction 1 − 1/n² of the flow speed, which Fresnel put down to partial ether drag; von Laue (1907) showed it is exactly the first-order relativistic addition of c/n and v.

name: Kerr multipole moments and the no-hair theorem
summary: A stationary spacetime has Geroch–Hansen mass and current multipole moments analogous to those of a static charge distribution; for Kerr all of them are fixed by M and a, so an independent measurement of the quadrupole −Ma² (EMRIs with LISA, ringdown spectroscopy, pulsar–black-hole timing) tests the no-hair theorem.

name: Multipole radiation: Larmor to the quadrupole formula
summary: Gravitational radiation is organized by the same multipole expansion as EM radiation, but conservation of mass and momentum removes the monopole and dipole terms, so the leading emission comes from the reduced mass quadrupole with power ∝ (d³Q/dt³)², paralleling Larmor's ∝ (d²p/dt²)².
map: P_{GW}=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle\ \leftrightarrow\ P_{EM}=\frac{\mu_0\ddot p^2}{6\pi c}
breaks: Gravity is spin-2 and has one sign of charge, so there is no dipole radiation; it is nonlinear, the radiated energy itself gravitates (Isaacson tensor, memory), and the expansion uses tensor rather than vector harmonics.

name: Superradiance: Kerr black hole as an amplifier
summary: Waves with ω < mΩ_H that scatter off a Kerr hole are amplified by tapping its rotation (Zel'dovich–Starobinsky superradiance, the wave form of the Penrose process); Bekenstein read this as stimulated emission paired with spontaneous Hawking emission, and a mirror or a massive field's own potential turns the gain into a laser-like 'black-hole bomb' instability.
breaks: The gain comes from horizon rotation, not population inversion, and it saturates as the hole spins down; ultralight-boson clouds (current research) radiate continuous GWs rather than light.

name: Stabilized lasers and Fabry–Pérot cavities in GW detectors
summary: Interferometric GW detection rests on laser engineering: 1064 nm Nd:YAG-based lasers frequency-stabilized by Pound–Drever–Hall locking, mode-cleaner cavities, km-scale Fabry–Pérot arms, and power/signal recycling that builds up hundreds of kW of circulating light, which sets the shot-noise floor.

name: Transformation optics: spacetime geometry as a medium
summary: Maxwell's equations on a curved spacetime, or in transformed coordinates, are the same as those in flat space with an impedance-matched anisotropic medium ε = μ (Plebanski; Gordon's optical metric for moving media); transformation optics inverts the map to design cloaks and metamaterial analogues of black holes, Einstein rings and cosmic strings.
breaks: Only light propagation on a fixed geometry is mimicked, with no gravitating dynamics; dispersion and loss restrict it to narrow bands, and g_{0i} ≠ 0 requires magnetoelectric coupling.
sources: Leonhardt (2006). "Optical Conformal Mapping". *Science* 312, 1777. [doi:10.1126/science.1126493](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1126493)

name: Fibre-optical event horizons and analogue Hawking light
summary: A soliton in a fibre raises the refractive index through the Kerr effect; in its co-moving frame, probe light slower than the pulse cannot cross the front, which forms black/white-hole horizon pairs, and the frequency conversion observed there is the stimulated analogue of Hawking emission.
breaks: Strong optical dispersion regularizes the trans-Planckian region, so the spectrum is not exactly thermal; there is no gravity, entropy or backreaction, and claims of spontaneous analogue Hawking photons in bulk glass are disputed.

name: Squeezed light from OPOs beats detector shot noise
summary: Optical parametric oscillators (χ(2) down-conversion below threshold) generate squeezed vacuum that is injected at the dark port, cutting shot noise by about 2–3 dB in LIGO and Virgo since O3; in O4 a 300 m filter cavity rotates the squeezing angle with frequency so that radiation-pressure noise is not raised at low frequency.
sources: Walls (1983). "Squeezed states of light". *Nature* 306, 141. [doi:10.1038/306141a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/306141a0)

name: Parametric down-conversion ≡ particle creation
summary: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion and Hawking, Unruh or cosmological particle creation are the same Bogoliubov transformation of mode operators: the output is a two-mode squeezed vacuum that looks thermal when one partner mode is traced out, with the temperature set by the squeeze parameter.
map: \hat b_1=\cosh r\,\hat a_1+\sinh r\,\hat a_2^\dagger,\ \langle n\rangle=\sinh^2r;\ \text{Hawking: }\tanh r=e^{-\pi\omega/\kappa}\ (\hbar=c=1)
breaks: In optics the pump is an external classical field acting through a χ(2) medium; in gravity the 'pump' is the spacetime geometry, and the partner modes lie behind a horizon.

name: Vacuum Cherenkov radiation bounds Lorentz violation
summary: Cherenkov emission needs v > c/n; if Lorentz violation made the vacuum photon phase speed lower than a particle's maximal speed, charged particles above a threshold would radiate in vacuum, so the survival of TeV–PeV electrons and protons from cosmic-ray and gamma-ray sources bounds Standard-Model-Extension coefficients.
sources: Colladay & Kostelecký (1998). "Lorentz-violating extension of the standard model". *Phys. Rev. D* 58, 116002. [doi:10.1103/physrevd.58.116002](https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevd.58.116002)

name: Dipole radiation as a signature of scalar–tensor gravity
summary: GR forbids gravitational dipole radiation, but in scalar–tensor theories bodies with different scalar charges (sensitivities) emit scalar dipole radiation at −1PN relative to the quadrupole, just as an EM dipole radiates when charge-to-mass ratios differ; binary-pulsar and GW inspiral timing bound it tightly.

name: Radiation reaction: Abraham–Lorentz vs 2.5PN
summary: Radiation back-reacts on its source: through the Abraham–Lorentz(–Dirac) force for charges and the Burke–Thorne 2.5PN potential for masses, whose integration gives the Peters–Mathews inspiral and chirp; the gravitational self-force programme (MiSaTaQuWa) mirrors the DeWitt–Brehme treatment of point charges.
breaks: EM reaction is dipolar (third time derivative) and gravitational reaction is quadrupolar (fifth derivative, 2.5PN); the gravitational self-force is gauge dependent, and the runaway solutions of ALD have no clean gravitational analogue.

name: Accelerated-charge radiation and the Unruh bath
summary: Seen from the co-accelerating frame, the Larmor radiation of a uniformly accelerated charge is emission and absorption of zero-energy Rindler photons from the thermal Unruh bath (Higuchi–Matsas–Sudarsky 1992); this ties a classical radiation formula to the Unruh effect and to the equivalence-principle puzzle of whether a supported charge radiates.

name: Black-hole scattering: partial waves, glory, orbiting
summary: Wave scattering by a black hole is solved with the partial-wave and Regge-pole methods of Mie theory; the cross section shows a backward glory and orbiting oscillations tied to the photon sphere, and in the eikonal limit its Regge poles are the quasinormal modes.
breaks: A black hole is a perfect absorber with a long-range 1/r potential (Coulomb-like phase, divergent forward cross section), unlike a finite dielectric sphere.

name: The four laws of black-hole mechanics
summary: Stationary black holes obey laws formally identical to the four laws of thermodynamics, with surface gravity as temperature and area as entropy. Hawking radiation made the identification physical, because κ really is a temperature of order ħκ/2πck_B.
map: dM=\frac{\kappa}{8\pi G}dA+\Omega_HdJ+\Phi_HdQ\ \leftrightarrow\ dU=TdS+\cdots;\ T_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi ck_B},\ S=\frac{k_Bc^3A}{4G\hbar}
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)
Wald (2001). "The Thermodynamics of Black Holes". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 4, 6. [arXiv:gr-qc/9912119](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9912119)

name: Generalized second law and negative heat capacity
summary: Bekenstein's generalized second law, d(S_outside+S_BH)≥0, extends the second law to horizons. A Schwarzschild black hole has negative heat capacity, C=-8πGM²k_B/ħc, so it heats up as it evaporates.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)

name: Tolman–Ehrenfest: temperature in a gravitational field
summary: In thermal equilibrium in a static spacetime, temperature is not uniform. The local temperature satisfies T√(-g_00)=const, so heat has weight and the zeroth law is modified by redshift. This is used for stellar and neutron-star interiors and is the local form of Hawking temperature redshifting.
sources: Tolman (1930). "On the Weight of Heat and Thermal Equilibrium in General Relativity". *Phys. Rev.* 35, 904. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.35.904](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.35.904)

name: Einstein's equations as an equation of state
summary: Jacobson derived Einstein's equations by imposing the Clausius relation δQ=TdS on every local Rindler horizon, using the Unruh temperature and area-entropy. This suggests that gravity is thermodynamics of underlying microscopic degrees of freedom; entropic-gravity proposals build on the idea but are contested.
map:
\delta Q=T\,dS,\ T= rac{\hbar a}{2\pi},\ S=\eta A\ \Rightarrow\ G_{\mu
u}+\Lambda g_{\mu
u}= rac{2\pi}{\hbar\eta}T_{\mu
u}
sources: Jacobson (1995). "Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 75, 1260. [arXiv:gr-qc/9504004](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9504004)

name: Black-hole chemistry: van der Waals-like P–V criticality
summary: With Λ treated as pressure P=-Λ/8πG and the black-hole mass as enthalpy, charged AdS black holes have a liquid–gas-like coexistence line ending at a critical point with mean-field exponents and a universal ratio P_cv_c/T_c=3/8. Holographic heat engines run cycles in this extended phase space.
breaks: The 'volume' is a thermodynamic conjugate rather than a container volume, there is no microscopic molecular picture, and treating Λ as a variable is itself an assumption. The resemblance to van der Waals extends to the mean-field equation of state only.
sources: Kubizňák & Mann (2012). "P-V criticality of charged AdS black holes". *JHEP* 07, 033. [arXiv:1205.0559](https://arxiv.org/abs/1205.0559)

name: Replica trick from spin glasses to replica wormholes
summary: The Page curve was computed by the replica trick: Rényi entropies Tr ρ^n from gravitational path integrals on n-fold covers, with replica wormholes as new saddles, then continued to n→1. The same analytic continuation in replica number powers spin-glass theory (n→0 for ⟨ln Z⟩).
sources: Penington et al. (2019). "Replica wormholes and the black hole interior". [arXiv:1911.11977](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.11977)
Almheiri et al. (2019). "Replica wormholes and the entropy of Hawking radiation". [arXiv:1911.12333](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.12333)
Parisi (1979). "Infinite Number of Order Parameters for Spin-Glasses". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 43, 1754. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.43.1754)

name: Euclidean gravity partition function
summary: Gibbons and Hawking computed black-hole thermodynamics from a canonical partition function: the Euclidean action of the black hole, smooth only if imaginary time has period ħ/k_BT_H, gives F=-k_BT ln Z and the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy. Negative heat capacity makes the flat-space canonical ensemble unstable unless the system is boxed (York) or in AdS.
map: Z=\int\mathcal Dg\,e^{-I_E[g]/\hbar}\approx e^{-I_E^{\text{cl}}},\ I_E=\beta M/2\Rightarrow S=\beta M-I_E=A/4G
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

name: LQG black-hole entropy from counting punctures
summary: In loop quantum gravity, horizon microstates are spin-network punctures carrying area quanta. Microcanonical counting gives S∝A, matching A/4 only for a specific Barbero–Immirzi parameter, with a universal -(3/2)ln A correction.
sources: Ashtekar et al. (1998). "Quantum Geometry and Black Hole Entropy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 80, 904. [arXiv:gr-qc/9710007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9710007)

name: Unruh effect: the vacuum as a Gibbs state
summary: Restricted to a Rindler wedge, the Minkowski vacuum is exactly a thermal density matrix of the boost generator (Bisognano–Wichmann), satisfying the KMS condition at T_U=ħa/2πck_B. Accelerated detectors respond with detailed-balance ratios e^{-ħω/k_BT_U}. De Sitter and black-hole horizons are thermal for the same reason: periodicity in imaginary time.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Bisognano & Wichmann (1976). "On the duality condition for quantum fields". *J. Math. Phys.* 17, 303. [doi:10.1063/1.522898](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.522898)

name: Microcanonical counting of black-hole microstates
summary: Strominger and Vafa counted the D-brane bound states with the charges of an extremal black hole and found S=ln Ω=A/4G exactly. It is a microcanonical-ensemble derivation of Bekenstein–Hawking entropy, done via the Cardy formula of the dual 2D CFT.
sources: Strominger & Vafa (1996). "Microscopic Origin of the Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy". *Phys. Lett. B* 379, 99. [arXiv:hep-th/9601029](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9601029)

name: Black holes as information-theoretic objects
summary: The black-hole branch uses information-theoretic entropy throughout: area as coarse-grained entropy, entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation, and the question of unitarity, which is a question about fine-grained (von Neumann) entropy.
sources: Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)

name: Bekenstein–Hawking entropy as missing information
summary: Bekenstein argued from information theory that a horizon must carry entropy proportional to its area, because information falling in is lost to outside observers. S_BH=A/4ℓ_P² is then the largest entropy any region can hold.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)

name: Page curve and the entropy of random states
summary: Page's theorem on the average entanglement entropy of a subsystem of a random pure state (nearly maximal until half the system) gives the Page curve. Unitary evaporation requires the radiation's fine-grained entropy to rise and then fall, unlike Hawking's monotonic thermal result.
sources: Page (1993). "Average entropy of a subsystem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 1291. [arXiv:gr-qc/9305007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305007)
Page (1993). "Information in black hole radiation". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 3743. [arXiv:hep-th/9306083](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9306083)
Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

name: Holographic principle and entropy bounds
summary: Black-hole entropy scaling with area rather than volume led to the Bekenstein bound and to the holographic principle of 't Hooft and Susskind: the number of degrees of freedom in a region is bounded by its boundary area in Planck units. This defeats naive extensive counting at gravitational scales.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)
't Hooft (1993). "Dimensional Reduction in Quantum Gravity". [arXiv:gr-qc/9310026](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9310026)
Susskind (1995). "The World as a Hologram". *J. Math. Phys.* 36, 6377. [arXiv:hep-th/9409089](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9409089)

name: Ryu–Takayanagi: entropy equals minimal area
summary: In AdS/CFT the von Neumann entropy of a boundary region equals the area of the minimal bulk surface anchored on it, divided by 4G. This generalizes Bekenstein–Hawking to arbitrary regions and makes entanglement the building block of geometry.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Hawking radiation is a Planck spectrum
summary: Bogoliubov mixing of in- and out-modes at a horizon gives exactly Bose–Einstein (Fermi–Dirac for fermions) occupation numbers at T_H, filtered by greybody factors. Evaporation is the Stefan–Boltzmann law applied to a horizon of area A.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: Relativistic kinetic theory and the Jüttner gas
summary: The relativistic Boltzmann equation has the Maxwell–Jüttner distribution as its equilibrium. Covariant kinetic theory underlies relativistic hydrodynamics, early-universe freeze-out and neutrino transport, and how temperature transforms under boosts (Planck–Einstein vs Ott) is still debated.

name: Thermal noise of interferometer test masses
summary: Brownian thermal noise of LIGO mirrors and coatings, often the limiting noise in the most sensitive band, is computed from the fluctuation–dissipation theorem. Levin's direct approach evaluates the dissipated power under a fictitious Gaussian pressure matching the laser beam profile.
sources: Levin (1998). "Internal thermal noise in the LIGO test masses: A direct approach". *Phys. Rev. D* 57, 659. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.57.659](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.57.659)
Callen & Welton (1951). "Irreversibility and Generalized Noise". *Phys. Rev.* 83, 34. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.83.34](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.83.34)

name: Kubo viscosity from horizons: η/s = ħ/4πk_B
summary: The shear viscosity of a strongly coupled plasma follows from the Kubo formula, the low-frequency limit of the stress-tensor retarded correlator, computed holographically as graviton absorption by a horizon. The result η/s=ħ/4πk_B is far below kinetic-theory estimates, which assume quasiparticles with mean free paths.
sources: Kovtun, Son & Starinets (2005). "Viscosity in Strongly Interacting Quantum Field Theories from Black Hole Physics". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 94, 111601. [arXiv:hep-th/0405231](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0405231)

name: Hawking–Page transition and deconfinement
summary: In AdS, thermal radiation and large black holes exchange dominance in a first-order Hawking–Page transition at T~1/ℓ_AdS. Via AdS/CFT this is the confinement/deconfinement transition of the dual large-N gauge theory, with free energy jumping from O(1) to O(N²).
sources: Hawking & Page (1983). "Thermodynamics of black holes in anti-de Sitter space". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 87, 577. [doi:10.1007/BF01208266](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01208266)
Witten (1998). "Anti-de Sitter space, thermal phase transition, and confinement in gauge theories". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 505. [arXiv:hep-th/9803131](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9803131)

name: Hagedorn temperature and the string phase transition
summary: String state densities grow exponentially with mass, ρ(m)~e^{m/T_H}, so the canonical partition function diverges at the Hagedorn temperature. This signals a phase transition (an analogue of deconfinement) rather than a true limiting temperature.
sources: Atick & Witten (1988). "The Hagedorn transition and the number of degrees of freedom of string theory". *Nucl. Phys. B* 310, 291. [doi:10.1016/0550-3213(88)90151-4](https://doi.org/10.1016/0550-3213(88)90151-4)

name: Choptuik critical collapse: universality and scaling
summary: At the threshold of black-hole formation, the final mass scales as M∝(p-p*)^γ with γ≈0.37 independent of the initial-data family. The critical solution is a self-similar attractor with a single unstable mode, so γ=1/λ like ν=1/y_t at an RG fixed point.
breaks: There is no thermal ensemble or fluctuation-driven criticality: it is deterministic PDE dynamics near a codimension-one fixed point, and the 'universality class' depends on the matter model (γ differs for radiation fluids).
sources: Choptuik (1993). "Universality and scaling in gravitational collapse of a massless scalar field". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 70, 9. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.9)

name: Holographic RG: the radial direction as scale
summary: In AdS/CFT the radial coordinate is an energy scale. The bulk Hamilton–Jacobi equations for radial evolution are RG flow equations of the boundary theory, and domain walls between AdS regions are RG flows between fixed points, with a holographic c-theorem.
map: \mu\frac{d g_i}{d\mu}=\beta_i(g)\ \leftrightarrow\ \text{radial flow of bulk fields }\phi_i(r),\ r\sim\ln\mu
sources: de Boer, Verlinde & Verlinde (2000). "On the Holographic Renormalization Group". *JHEP* 08, 003. [arXiv:hep-th/9912012](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9912012)

name: Asymptotic safety: a Wilson–Fisher fixed point for gravity
summary: Asymptotic safety applies Wilson's RG to gravity: a non-Gaussian UV fixed point of Newton's coupling with finitely many relevant directions would make gravity predictive, just as a critical fixed point has finitely many relevant scaling fields.

name: Clocks resolve the gravitational redshift
summary: Optical lattice and ion clocks at 1e-18 measure the GR redshift over cm (now sub-mm) heights, turning a classic GR test into a table-top AMO measurement and enabling chronometric geodesy.
sources: Chou et al. (2010). "Optical Clocks and Relativity". *Science* 329, 1630. [doi:10.1126/science.1192720](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1192720)
Bothwell et al. (2022). "Resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample". *Nature* 602, 420. [arXiv:2109.12238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12238)
Ludlow et al. (2015). "Optical atomic clocks". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 87, 637. [arXiv:1407.3493](https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.3493)

name: Quantum tests of the equivalence principle
summary: Matter-wave interferometry tests free-fall universality and gravitational phase shifts with quantum probes: the COW neutron experiment, then dual-species atom interferometers comparing isotopes.
sources: Colella, Overhauser & Werner (1975). "Observation of Gravitationally Induced Quantum Interference". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 34, 1472. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.34.1472)
Dimopoulos et al. (2007). "Testing General Relativity with Atom Interferometry". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 98, 111102. [arXiv:gr-qc/0610047](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0610047)

name: Atomic time underlies pulsar timing
summary: Pulsar arrival times are referenced to atomic time; clock-standard errors appear as a monopolar correlated residual distinct from the quadrupolar Hellings-Downs signature, and pulsar ensembles can cross-check atomic time scales.
sources: Hobbs et al. (2012). "Development of a pulsar-based time-scale". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 427, 2780. [arXiv:1208.3560](https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.3560)

name: Atom interferometers and clocks as GW detectors
summary: Proposed mid-band (0.01-10 Hz) detectors replace laser arms by light-pulse atom interferometry or clock comparisons between distant ensembles, using single-photon transitions to cancel laser phase noise.
sources: Graham et al. (2013). "New Method for Gravitational Wave Detection with Atomic Sensors". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 171102. [arXiv:1206.0818](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.0818)
Kolkowitz et al. (2016). "Gravitational wave detection with optical lattice atomic clocks". *Phys. Rev. D* 94, 124043. [arXiv:1606.01859](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.01859)

name: Clock comparisons as Lorentz-symmetry tests
summary: Ion and lattice clocks and entangled ion pairs bound Standard-Model-Extension coefficients through sidereal modulation of transition frequencies; clock pairs also measured time dilation at m/s speeds.
sources: Sanner et al. (2019). "Optical clock comparison for Lorentz symmetry testing". *Nature* 567, 204. [doi:10.1038/s41586-019-0972-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-0972-2)
Pruttivarasin et al. (2015). "Michelson–Morley analogue for electrons using trapped ions to test Lorentz symmetry". *Nature* 517, 592. [doi:10.1038/nature14091](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14091)
Kostelecký & Russell (2011). "Data tables for Lorentz and CPT violation". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 83, 11. [arXiv:0801.0287](https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0287)

name: Acoustic horizons and analogue Hawking radiation
summary: Bogoliubov phonons in a flowing BEC propagate on an acoustic metric; where flow exceeds sound speed a horizon forms and thermal, entangled phonon pairs are emitted. Curated in the analogue-gravity theme.
breaks: Kinematics only: no Einstein dynamics or backreaction; Bogoliubov dispersion breaks Lorentz invariance at the healing length; nK signals sit on thermal noise.
sources: Unruh (1981). "Experimental Black-Hole Evaporation?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 46, 1351. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.46.1351)

Steinhauer (2016). "Observation of quantum Hawking radiation and its entanglement in an analogue black hole". *Nature Phys.* 12, 959. [arXiv:1510.00621](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.00621)

name: BEC simulators of cosmological particle creation
summary: Rapidly expanding ring BECs and modulated condensates emulate particle creation in expanding spacetimes and Unruh radiation, testing QFT-in-curved-spacetime kinematics with phonons.
breaks: Effective metric only; condensate dissipation and nonlinearity have no curved-spacetime counterpart.
sources: Eckel et al. (2018). "A Rapidly Expanding Bose-Einstein Condensate: An Expanding Universe in the Lab". *Phys. Rev. X* 8, 021021. [arXiv:1710.05800](https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.05800)
Hu et al. (2019). "Quantum simulation of Unruh radiation". *Nature Phys.* 15, 785. [arXiv:1807.07504](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.07504)

name: Quantum foundations meets quantum gravity
summary: Tabletop tests of the quantum nature of gravity (gravity-induced entanglement, gravitational collapse) grew out of foundations research and tie the measurement problem to the quantum status of spacetime.
sources: Bose et al. (2017). "Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240401. [arXiv:1707.06050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06050)
Penrose (1996). "On Gravity's role in Quantum State Reduction". *Gen. Rel. Grav.* 28, 581. [doi:10.1007/BF02105068](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02105068)

name: Bell tests need spacelike separation
summary: Bell's local causality is defined by light cones; loophole-free tests choose settings and record outcomes at spacelike separation, and no-signalling keeps quantum nonlocality compatible with relativity.
sources: Aspect, Dalibard & Roger (1982). "Experimental Test of Bell's Inequalities Using Time-Varying Analyzers". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 49, 1804. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1804](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.49.1804)
Hensen et al. (2015). "Loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins separated by 1.3 kilometres". *Nature* 526, 682. [arXiv:1508.05949](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05949)

name: Proper-time which-path decoherence
summary: A clock in superposition at two heights records which-path proper time, so interferometric visibility drops; gravitational time dilation gives a universal decoherence for composite systems with internal dynamics.

Pikovski, Zych, Costa & Brukner (2015). "Universal decoherence due to gravitational time dilation". *Nature Phys.* 11, 668. [arXiv:1311.1095](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1095)

summary: Superpositions of distinct mass distributions are proposed to collapse at a rate set by the gravitational self-energy of their difference: a dynamical answer to the measurement problem, testable with massive superpositions.

name: Black-hole evaporation as an open quantum system
summary: Treating hole plus radiation as a bipartite quantum system lets open-system and entropy tools (reduced density matrices, Renyi entropies, replica trick) diagnose unitarity; the Page curve is the radiation's entanglement entropy.

name: Quasinormal modes as non-Hermitian spectra
summary: Outgoing boundary conditions make the black-hole perturbation operator non-self-adjoint; quasinormal modes are resonances whose pseudospectrum shows the spectral instability familiar from non-Hermitian physics.
sources: Jaramillo, Panosso Macedo & Al Sheikh (2021). "Pseudospectrum and Black Hole Quasinormal Mode Instability". *Phys. Rev. X* 11, 031003. [arXiv:2004.06434](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.06434)

name: Black holes as fastest scramblers
summary: Black holes scramble information in a time ~ (beta/2pi) ln S and saturate the Maldacena-Shenker-Stanford bound on the OTOC Lyapunov exponent; Hayden-Preskill shows information thrown in after the Page time re-emerges after one scrambling time.
sources: Maldacena, Shenker & Stanford (2016). "A bound on chaos". *JHEP* 08, 106. [arXiv:1503.01409](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01409)

summary: The Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model of N Majoranas with random all-to-all couplings is maximally chaotic, and its low-energy Schwarzian sector matches Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity in near-AdS2: a solvable bridge between quantum chaos and holography.

name: Bekenstein bound from relative entropy
summary: Quantum-information thermodynamics (positivity of relative entropy) gives a precise statement and proof of the Bekenstein bound and underpins the generalized second law.
sources: Casini (2008). "Relative entropy and the Bekenstein bound". *Class. Quantum Grav.* 25, 205021. [arXiv:0804.2182](https://arxiv.org/abs/0804.2182)

name: Entanglement area law and black-hole entropy
summary: Tracing out field modes inside a surface gives an entanglement entropy proportional to its area with a cutoff-dependent coefficient, a candidate microscopic contribution to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy.

name: Page curve, monogamy and the firewall
summary: Page's typical-subsystem entropy gives the rise and fall of radiation entropy; monogamy of entanglement forbids late Hawking modes being maximally entangled with both early radiation and interior partners (the AMPS firewall).
sources: Page (1993). "Average entropy of a subsystem". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 71, 1291. [arXiv:gr-qc/9305007](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9305007)

name: Ryu-Takayanagi: entanglement equals area
summary: Boundary entanglement entropy of a region equals the minimal bulk surface area in Planck units; entanglement builds connected spacetime, and MERA tensor networks give a discrete toy bulk.
sources: Ryu & Takayanagi (2006). "Holographic Derivation of Entanglement Entropy from AdS/CFT". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602. [arXiv:hep-th/0603001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/0603001)

name: Gravity-mediated entanglement witness (BMV)
summary: LOCC cannot create entanglement, so if two masses in superposition become entangled through gravity alone, gravity cannot act as a classical channel; the proposed test is a direct application of entanglement monotonicity.
sources: Bose et al. (2017). "Spin Entanglement Witness for Quantum Gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240401. [arXiv:1707.06050](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06050)

Marletto & Vedral (2017). "Gravitationally-induced entanglement between two massive particles is sufficient evidence of quantum effects in gravity". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 119, 240402. [arXiv:1707.06036](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.06036)

name: Holographic complexity
summary: Quantum circuit complexity is conjectured to be dual to the growing volume or action of the black-hole interior (complexity = volume or action).
sources: Susskind (2016). "Computational complexity and black hole horizons". *Fortsch. Phys.* 64, 24. [arXiv:1403.5695](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5695)

name: Quantum repeaters for VLBI baselines
summary: Distributing entanglement between telescopes would allow optical interferometry with arbitrarily long baselines without transporting photons, a possible extension of EHT-style imaging to optical wavelengths.
sources: Gottesman, Jennewein & Croke (2012). "Longer-Baseline Telescopes Using Quantum Repeaters". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 109, 070503. [arXiv:1107.2939](https://arxiv.org/abs/1107.2939)

name: Holographic codes: bulk locality as QEC
summary: Bulk operators in AdS/CFT can be reconstructed on many boundary subregions, exactly as logical operators of an erasure-correcting code; perfect-tensor (HaPPY) codes reproduce RT and entanglement-wedge reconstruction.
map: \mathcal H_{\rm bulk}\hookrightarrow\mathcal H_{\rm code}\subset\mathcal H_{\rm CFT};\ \text{RT}\leftrightarrow\text{min-cut}

summary: Quantum processors have emulated SYK-like teleportation protocols interpreted as traversable wormholes; the 2022 superconducting-processor claim is contested because the learned Hamiltonian may not be holographic.

name: SU(2) recoupling builds spin networks
summary: Loop quantum gravity labels spin-network edges by SU(2) irreps and nodes by intertwiners; the area spectrum is the SU(2) Casimir and spin-foam amplitudes use 6j symbols from angular-momentum recoupling.
sources: Rovelli & Smolin (1995). "Discreteness of area and volume in quantum gravity". *Nucl. Phys. B* 442, 593. [arXiv:gr-qc/9411005](https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/9411005)

name: Spinors, Lorentz group and Thomas precession
summary: Spin-1/2 is a representation of SL(2,C), the double cover of the Lorentz group; Thomas precession (a Wigner rotation) supplies the factor 1/2 in atomic spin-orbit coupling, and the Dirac equation gives g=2 and fine structure.
sources: Thomas (1926). "The Motion of the Spinning Electron". *Nature* 117, 514. [doi:10.1038/117514a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/117514a0)
Dirac (1928). "The quantum theory of the electron". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 117, 610. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1928.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1928.0023)

name: Hawking radiation as WKB tunnelling
summary: The emission rate can be computed as a semiclassical tunnelling probability across the horizon; energy conservation gives small non-thermal corrections.
sources: Parikh & Wilczek (2000). "Hawking radiation as tunneling". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 85, 5042. [arXiv:hep-th/9907001](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9907001)

name: Poschl-Teller and WKB models of ringdown
summary: Black-hole perturbations obey a Schrodinger-like Regge-Wheeler/Zerilli equation; replacing the barrier by an exactly solvable Poschl-Teller potential, or expanding it by WKB, gives the quasinormal ringdown frequencies.
sources: Ferrari & Mashhoon (1984). "New approach to the quasinormal modes of a black hole". *Phys. Rev. D* 30, 295. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.30.295)

name: Berry connection vs Levi-Civita connection
summary: The Berry phase is the holonomy of a U(1) connection on parameter space, as a vector's rotation after parallel transport is the holonomy of the Levi-Civita connection; both are connections with curvature on fibre bundles.
breaks: Berry curvature is a non-dynamical abelian field on Hilbert-space parameters; spacetime curvature is a dynamical SO(3,1) connection fixed by Einstein's equations.
sources: Berry (1984). "Quantal phase factors accompanying adiabatic changes". *Proc. R. Soc. A* 392, 45. [doi:10.1098/rspa.1984.0023](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1984.0023)

name: Gravitational Aharonov-Bohm effect
summary: Atom interferometers measured a gravitational phase shift on wavepackets that feel no net gravitational force, the gravitational counterpart of the Aharonov-Bohm effect.
sources: Overstreet et al. (2022). "Observation of a gravitational Aharonov-Bohm effect". *Science* 375, 226. [doi:10.1126/science.abl7152](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abl7152)

name: Euclidean path integral gives the Hawking temperature
summary: Wick-rotating the black-hole metric and demanding regularity at the horizon forces periodic imaginary time, identical to the thermal path-integral period; the Euclidean action gives the partition function and entropy.
sources: Gibbons & Hawking (1977). "Action integrals and partition functions in quantum gravity". *Phys. Rev. D* 15, 2752. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.15.2752)

name: No-boundary wavefunction of the universe
summary: Hartle and Hawking define the state of the universe as a Euclidean path integral over compact geometries, transplanting semiclassical and instanton machinery from QM to quantum cosmology.
sources: Hartle & Hawking (1983). "Wave function of the Universe". *Phys. Rev. D* 28, 2960. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960)

name: Problem of time and relational evolution
summary: Canonical quantum gravity imposes the Wheeler-DeWitt constraint H|Psi>=0, so there is no external time; the Page-Wootters mechanism recovers Schrodinger dynamics as correlations between a clock subsystem and the rest.
sources: DeWitt (1967). "Quantum Theory of Gravity. I. The Canonical Theory". *Phys. Rev.* 160, 1113. [doi:10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.160.1113)
Page & Wootters (1983). "Evolution without evolution: Dynamics described by stationary observables". *Phys. Rev. D* 27, 2885. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.27.2885](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.27.2885)

name: Black-hole scattering and partial waves
summary: Wave scattering off Schwarzschild and Kerr holes uses partial-wave phase shifts, greybody factors and absorption cross sections from quantum scattering theory; rotating holes superradiantly amplify modes with omega < m Omega_H.

name: Standard quantum limit of interferometry
summary: A GW interferometer is a quantum-optical measurement whose sensitivity is set by the trade-off between photon shot noise and radiation-pressure back-action, the standard quantum limit.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)

name: Dynamical Casimir effect in circuit QED
summary: Modulating a superconducting resonator's boundary condition with a SQUID at GHz rates creates photon pairs from vacuum, the same parametric particle creation as moving mirrors and cosmological particle production.
sources: Wilson et al. (2011). "Observation of the dynamical Casimir effect in a superconducting circuit". *Nature* 479, 376. [arXiv:1105.4714](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.4714)

name: LIGO mirrors as optomechanical systems
summary: Interferometer test masses are radiation-pressure-coupled oscillators: optical springs, parametric instabilities, ponderomotive squeezing and feedback cooling of 10 kg mirrors toward the motional ground state are cavity optomechanics at kg scale.
sources: Whittle et al. (2021). "Approaching the motional ground state of a 10-kg object". *Science* 372, 1333. [arXiv:2102.12665](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.12665)
Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg & Marquardt (2014). "Cavity optomechanics". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 86, 1391. [arXiv:1303.0733](https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.0733)

name: Optomechanical probes of Planck-scale physics
summary: Quantum-optical control of massive oscillators can bound deformed canonical commutators (minimal-length models) and test gravity-related collapse in macroscopic superpositions.
sources: Pikovski et al. (2012). "Probing Planck-scale physics with quantum optics". *Nature Phys.* 8, 393. [arXiv:1111.1979](https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.1979)

name: Unruh-DeWitt detector is a two-level atom
summary: The detector used to define Unruh and Hawking radiation is a two-level system coupled to a quantum field, the atom-field model of quantum optics; accelerated detectors see thermal photon statistics.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Crispino, Higuchi & Matsas (2008). "The Unruh effect and its applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 787. [arXiv:0710.5373](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5373)

name: Quantum metrology for GW astronomy
summary: Gravitational-wave science drives squeezing at audio frequencies and filter-cavity development; the detectors are the most sensitive deployed quantum-enhanced instruments.
sources: Tse et al. (2019). "Quantum-Enhanced Advanced LIGO Detectors in the Era of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 231107. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.231107)

name: Squeezed-light injection in GW detectors
summary: Injecting squeezed vacuum into the dark port lowers shot noise below the standard quantum limit; frequency-dependent squeezing also cuts radiation-pressure noise. Used in LIGO and Virgo observing runs since 2019.
sources: Caves (1981). "Quantum-mechanical noise in an interferometer". *Phys. Rev. D* 23, 1693. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.23.1693)

name: Unruh/Hawking vacuum as two-mode squeezing
summary: The Bogoliubov transformation between Minkowski and Rindler (or in and out) modes is exactly a two-mode squeezing operator; the Minkowski vacuum is a two-mode squeezed state across the horizon, thermal on either side.
sources: Unruh (1976). "Notes on black-hole evaporation". *Phys. Rev. D* 14, 870. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.14.870)
Crispino, Higuchi & Matsas (2008). "The Unruh effect and its applications". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 80, 787. [arXiv:0710.5373](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5373)

name: Black-hole shadows and S2 orbit as strong-field tests
summary: The EHT ring diameters of M87* and Sgr A* agree with the Kerr shadow size, which barely depends on spin, to about 10%, giving a strong-field test of the metric. GRAVITY/VLTI and Keck tracking of the star S2 around Sgr A* measured the combined gravitational redshift and transverse Doppler shift, and the Schwarzschild periastron precession.
breaks: The ring is emission from plasma, not the shadow edge itself. Its calibration relies on GRMHD models and on mass priors, which limits how far the test can reach.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Relativistic beaming in black-hole images and jets
summary: The brightness asymmetry of the EHT rings of M87* and Sgr A* comes largely from Doppler boosting of plasma orbiting at close to c. Apparent superluminal motion in AGN jets follows from the light-travel-time kinematics of relativistic ejecta. Both are special-relativistic kinematics layered on top of curved-spacetime ray tracing.
breaks: Near the horizon, Doppler and gravitational redshift do not separate, so full GR ray tracing replaces the flat-space formulas.
sources: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (2019). "First M87 Event Horizon Telescope Results. I. The Shadow of the Supermassive Black Hole". *Astrophys. J. Lett.* 875, L1. [arXiv:1906.11238](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.11238)

name: Energy conditions, area theorem and generalized 2nd law
summary: Through the Raychaudhuri equation and the Einstein equations, the null energy condition makes horizon area non-decreasing (Hawking's area theorem, the 'second law'). Hawking radiation carries a negative energy flux across the horizon, so it violates the NEC and the area can shrink. Bekenstein's generalized second law then replaces the area theorem.
sources: Bekenstein (1973). "Black Holes and Entropy". *Phys. Rev. D* 7, 2333. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevD.7.2333)

name: Testing Hawking's area theorem with merger signals
summary: The inspiral gives the component masses and spins and the ringdown gives the remnant's mass and spin, so the horizon areas before and after merger can be compared. Analyses of GW150914 and later high-SNR events find A_f > A₁ + A₂ with high confidence. This is an observational test of the second law of black-hole mechanics.

name: AdS black holes as thermal CFT states (Hawking–Page)
summary: In AdS/CFT a large AdS–Schwarzschild black hole is dual to the boundary CFT at temperature T_H, with entropy A/4G equal to the CFT's thermal entropy. The Hawking–Page transition between thermal AdS and the black hole maps to the confinement/deconfinement transition of the gauge theory, and quasinormal decay maps to thermalization.
map: T_H=T_{\rm CFT},\ S_{BH}=\frac{A}{4G}=S_{\rm CFT};\ \ T_{\rm HP}=\frac{3}{2\pi\ell}\ (\text{AdS}_5,\ \hbar=c=k_B=1)\leftrightarrow T_{\rm deconf}
breaks: Small AdS black holes have negative heat capacity and are unstable, like asymptotically flat ones. The duality is cleanest at large N and strong coupling.
sources: Maldacena (1998). "The Large N Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity". *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2, 231. [arXiv:hep-th/9711200](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9711200)

name: Horizon area quanta and black-hole entropy in LQG
summary: LQG's discrete area spectrum lets one count the spin-network punctures of an isolated horizon. The count gives an entropy proportional to area, which equals A/4 only for one value of the Barbero–Immirzi parameter (γ ≈ 0.24–0.27, depending on the counting scheme). It also predicts a universal −(3/2) ln A correction.
breaks: Matching A/4 requires fixing γ by hand, and Hawking radiation itself has not been derived from the LQG dynamics.

name: Hawking radiation as curved-spacetime particle creation
summary: Hawking radiation is a result of QFT in curved spacetime. The in-vacuum of a collapsing geometry, carried through the horizon's exponential redshift, is thermal for late-time observers. Its Bogoliubov coefficients give a Planck spectrum at T_H = ħκ/2πck_B, and the same calculation gives cosmological particle creation and the Unruh effect.
sources: Hawking (1975). "Particle creation by black holes". *Commun. Math. Phys.* 43, 199. [doi:10.1007/BF02345020](https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02345020)

name: D-brane microstate counting reproduces A/4G
summary: Strominger and Vafa counted BPS bound states of D-branes that carry the charges of a five-dimensional extremal black hole. Their degeneracy reproduces the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy exactly, the first statistical-mechanical derivation of black-hole entropy. Near-extremal extensions also reproduce Hawking emission with the correct greybody factors.
breaks: The count is controlled only for supersymmetric or near-extremal black holes. Schwarzschild-like black holes far from extremality are not covered.
sources: Strominger & Vafa (1996). "Microscopic Origin of the Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy". *Phys. Lett. B* 379, 99. [arXiv:hep-th/9601029](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-th/9601029)

name: Islands and the Page curve from holographic entropy
summary: The Ryu–Takayanagi formula, extended to quantum extremal surfaces, computes the entropy of black-hole radiation. For an evaporating black hole coupled to a bath, a new extremal surface (an island) appears after the Page time, and the entropy then follows the unitary Page curve. AdS/CFT also gives the main argument that evaporation is unitary, because the dual CFT evolves unitarily.
breaks: The derivations are cleanest in AdS or in low-dimensional JT-gravity models. How information gets out in a local, operational sense, and the status of the result in asymptotically flat spacetime, are still debated.
sources: Penington (2020). "Entanglement wedge reconstruction and the information paradox". *JHEP* 09, 002. [arXiv:1905.08255](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08255)

Almheiri, Engelhardt, Marolf & Maxfield (2019). "The entropy of bulk quantum fields and the entanglement wedge of an evaporating black hole". *JHEP* 12, 063. [arXiv:1905.08762](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.08762)

name: Semiclassical origin of the paradox and of islands
summary: Hawking's 1976 non-unitarity argument comes from QFT in curved spacetime. The late-time radiation is entangled with partner modes behind the horizon, so its fine-grained entropy grows without bound. The island formula keeps the same semiclassical ingredient, the generalized entropy A/4Għ + S_bulk, but extremizes over gravitational saddles (replica wormholes), so the Page curve emerges without new local physics.

name: Schwarzschild and Kerr as exact vacuum solutions
summary: The black-hole note studies the horizons, ergospheres and geodesics of the same metrics the exact-solutions note derives. Schwarzschild is the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution (Birkhoff), Kerr is its rotating generalisation, and Reissner–Nordström and Kerr–Newman are the charged versions. Uniqueness theorems make Kerr–Newman the stationary end state of collapse (no-hair).

name: No-hair theorems vs black-hole scalarization
summary: In GR the no-hair and uniqueness theorems force stationary vacuum black holes to be Kerr, and many scalar–tensor theories also admit Kerr. Einstein–scalar–Gauss–Bonnet couplings, motivated by string α′ corrections, evade the theorems through spontaneous scalarization and give hairy black holes. Their deviations from Kerr are targets for ringdown and imaging tests.
breaks: Scalarized solutions can be unstable, and some of these theories have ill-posed evolution equations. Current observations do not distinguish them from Kerr.

name: Kerr quasinormal modes set the merger ringdown
summary: A merger remnant rings down as a sum of damped Kerr quasinormal modes, whose complex frequencies follow from Teukolsky perturbation theory and depend only on the final mass and spin. Measuring two or more modes over-determines (M, a) and so tests the no-hair theorem (black-hole spectroscopy).

breaks: Linear QNMs fail near the merger peak, where nonlinear mode couplings and overtone fits are still contested.
